new.title: Visit the Sleeping Beauty castle at Sababurg
new.desc: Burg Sababurg in the Reinhardswald near Hofgeismar was built from 1334 and is known as the Dornröschenschloss, the setting linked to the Grimm fairy tale of Sleeping Beauty. The ruined hunting lodge of the Landgraves of Hesse now houses a hotel and restaurant.
new.tip: The rose garden and courtyard are best seen in early summer. Combine the visit with the nearby Tierpark and Urwald.

new.title: Walk among ancient oaks in the Urwald Sababurg
new.desc: The Urwald Sababurg is one of Germany's oldest protected forest reserves, set aside in 1907 in the Reinhardswald. Gnarled oaks and beeches several centuries old stand among dead wood left to decay naturally.
new.tip: A signposted circular path starts near the Sababurg car park. Wear sturdy shoes, as the ground is uneven and damp.

new.title: See Rapunzel's tower at Burg Trendelburg
new.desc: Burg Trendelburg above the Diemel valley dates back to the 13th century and is linked with the Rapunzel fairy tale. The castle is still used as a hotel and has a well-known tower with a long-haired figure.
new.tip: The courtyard can be visited for a small fee; check opening times in the hotel reception. Parking is below the castle.

new.title: Stroll through Schloss Wilhelmsthal's rococo park
new.desc: Schloss Wilhelmsthal near Calden was built from 1743 to 1761 for Landgrave Wilhelm VIII to designs by François de Cuvilliés. It is one of the most important rococo palaces in Germany and is surrounded by an English landscape park.
new.tip: Guided tours of the interiors run in the season; the park is free to enter. Part of the Museumslandschaft Hessen Kassel.

new.title: Admire the Baroque harbour of Bad Karlshafen
new.desc: Bad Karlshafen on the Weser was founded in 1699 by Landgrave Karl as a planned Huguenot town. Its rectangular harbour basin, intended to link the Weser with a canal to Kassel, is lined by baroque white houses.
new.tip: Walk around the basin and visit the Deutsches Hugenotten-Museum. Evenings are quiet with a few places to sit by the water.

new.title: Visit the Romanesque Dom St. Peter in Fritzlar
new.desc: The Dom St. Peter in Fritzlar goes back to a monastery founded by Boniface in the 8th century; the present church is largely 12th to 14th century. Its cloister and cathedral treasury hold medieval goldsmith work.
new.tip: The church is usually open during the day. The Domschatz and the cloister are visited separately.
new.q: Dom St. Peter, Am Domplatz, Fritzlar

new.title: Photograph the half-timbered market square in Homberg (Efze)
new.desc: Homberg (Efze) has one of Hesse's best-preserved half-timbered old towns, around the market square with the Marienkirche above it. The Reformation Landtag of 1526 was held here, and the hilltop castle ruin looks over the Efze valley.
new.tip: Climb the steps to the Marienkirche for the view. The town is part of the Fachwerkstraße.

new.title: Watch the Bartenwetzer at Melsungen's half-timbered town hall
new.desc: The half-timbered Rathaus of Melsungen from 1555 stands free on the market square. Since 1928 a mechanical Bartenwetzer figure appears twice daily, at noon and 6 p.m., from the tower.
new.tip: Be on the market square just before noon to see the figure. The old town is compact and walkable.

new.title: Explore the Ziegenhain fortress and Schwalm museum
new.desc: Ziegenhain in Schwalmstadt was fortified as a Renaissance fortress by the Landgraves of Hesse in the 16th century. Its ramparts and moat survive, and the Museum der Schwalm shows regional costume and folk culture.
new.tip: Walk the ramparts and the old town streets first. Museum hours are limited outside the main season.

new.title: Stand on the Edersee dam wall
new.desc: The Edertalsperre was built from 1908 to 1914 and is one of Germany's largest dams, holding back the Edersee. The wall is 48 metres high and 400 metres long, and was breached in 1943 in the Dambusters raid before being rebuilt.
new.tip: You can walk across the top for free. In dry autumns low water reveals the old Asel village remains in the lake.

new.title: Look over the Edersee from Schloss Waldeck
new.desc: Schloss Waldeck stands high above the northern shore of the Edersee. The castle dates to the 12th century and was the seat of the Counts of Waldeck; it is now a hotel with the Schlossmuseum nearby.
new.tip: Come for the view and lake panorama. Park in the village below and walk up.

new.title: Tour the Residenzschloss in Bad Arolsen
new.desc: The Residenzschloss Arolsen was built from 1710 for the Princes of Waldeck, modelled loosely on Versailles. It has a large baroque park and the Christian Daniel Rauch museum honours the sculptor born in the town.
new.tip: The palace is visited by guided tour; check dates before travelling. The park is free.

new.title: Explore the Gothic monastery church at Kloster Haina
new.desc: Kloster Haina was founded in 1215 and its Gothic church is considered one of the finest early Gothic buildings in Hesse. After the Reformation the grounds became a hospital for the sick and now serve as a hospital and museum site.
new.tip: The church is open for visitors in daytime; the monastery museum has set hours.

new.title: Count the ten towers of Frankenberg's Rathaus
new.desc: The Rathaus of Frankenberg an der Eder was built in 1509 and is crowned by ten slate-covered towers. It sits in a half-timbered old town above the Eder, with the Liebfrauenkirche close by.
new.tip: Photograph the Rathaus from the Obermarkt. Guided town walks are offered by the tourist office.

new.title: Tour the UNESCO Carolingian Westwork at Corvey
new.desc: Corvey Abbey near Höxter was founded in 822 and its Carolingian Westwork of 873 to 885 became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014. The former Benedictine abbey later became a princely residence and holds a large library.
new.tip: The abbey church and the Westwork can be visited, with a separate ticket for the museum. The poet Hoffmann von Fallersleben is buried here.

new.title: Admire the Weser Renaissance houses of Höxter
new.desc: Höxter's old town is full of half-timbered and Weser Renaissance buildings, including the Dechanei, the Fachwerkhaus at the Weser and the Kilianikirche. The Kiliani tower is a landmark of the town on the river.
new.tip: Start at the Kilianikirche and walk down to the river promenade. The Tourist-Information on Westerbachstraße gives a walking map.

new.title: Walk the old town and Landgrafenschloss of Eschwege
new.desc: Eschwege on the Werra grew around the Landgrafenschloss, a Renaissance palace with a notable Treppenturm from the 16th century. The old town has half-timbered houses, a Dünzebach nearby and the Leuchtberg view tower.
new.tip: The Schloss courtyard is free to enter. The tourist info is on the market square.

new.title: Visit Burg Ludwigstein above the Werra valley
new.desc: Burg Ludwigstein near Witzenhausen was built in the 15th century on a spur above the Werra. Since 1920 it has been a youth hostel and an archive of the German youth movement.
new.tip: Open to day visitors; the castle inn serves drinks and meals. The view from the courtyard is the main draw.

new.title: Stand inside the Stiftsruine in Bad Hersfeld
new.desc: The Stiftsruine of Bad Hersfeld is the largest Romanesque church ruin in the world. The abbey church was built in the 11th century and burned in 1761 during the Seven Years' War. It is the stage of the Bad Hersfelder Festspiele.
new.tip: The ruin is open in daytime. Tickets for the festival summer run from late June into August.

new.title: Visit the Salzmuseum in Bad Sooden-Allendorf
new.desc: The Salzmuseum at Söder Tor covers the history of salt production in Sooden, which was boiled from brine for centuries. It includes tools, models and the story of the town's salt trade and spa culture.
new.tip: Small museum, open weekends and holidays 14:00 to 17:00, plus Wednesdays in April to October. Admission is about one euro.

new.title: Eat Kartoffel-Lauchsuppe with Ahle Wurscht at Knallhütte
new.desc: Brauhaus Knallhütte in Baunatal is a brewery and beer garden in a historic setting; brewing here is dated back to 1752. The menu includes hearty portions, schnitzel and regional dishes.
new.tip: Try the potato and leek soup with Ahle Wurscht and a house beer. Open daily, shorter hours on Sundays; check ahead.

new.title: Taste Ahle Wurscht at Landfleischerei Koch in Calden
new.desc: Landfleischerei Koch in Calden is a well-known maker of Nordhessische Ahle Wurscht, the hard air-dried pork sausage that has had EU protected origin since 2023. The family butcher sells it with other regional sausages.
new.tip: Buy a sausage to take away and eat it with dark bread. Opening hours follow the shop, so check before going.

new.title: Drink organic Kellerbier at Schinkels Brauhaus
new.desc: Schinkels Brauhaus in Witzenhausen opened in 1997 and is credited as Hesse's first organic brewery. The family also bakes bread on site and the small brewpub serves food with its own beers.
new.tip: Order the Kellerbier or the cherry beer, a nod to Witzenhausen's cherry orchards. Hours vary, so check the website.

new.title: Dine on regional cooking at Stern's Restaurant
new.desc: Stern's Restaurant at the Romantik Hotel Zum Stern on the Linggplatz is listed in the Michelin Guide for regional cooking with international touches. The panelled dining rooms are in one of the oldest hotels in Hesse.
new.tip: Order the regional seasonal menu; book ahead for evenings.

new.title: Have Torte at Café Hetzler on Fritzlar's market square
new.desc: Café Hetzler is a long-standing café and Konditorei on the historic market square of Fritzlar. It offers cakes, pastries and tortes and doubles as a restaurant.
new.tip: Pick a slice of Torte from the counter. It closes around 18:00.

new.title: Eat homemade cake at Café Alt-Willingen
new.desc: Café Alt-Willingen on the Orenberg is known for its homemade cakes baked in-house. It has a panorama view over Willingen and the surrounding Upland hills.
new.tip: Choose a slice of cake and sit by the window or terrace for the view.

new.title: Eat regional dishes at SonneStuben on Frankenberg's market square
new.desc: SonneStuben at Marktplatz 2 in Frankenberg (Eder) is listed by the Michelin Guide for regional cooking. It has a terrace overlooking the market square and the town hall.
new.tip: Sit on the terrace in summer. Lunch is also served.

new.title: Order regional meat dishes at Zum Schiffchen in Wolfhagen
new.desc: Hotel and Restaurant Zum Schiffchen has been run since 1987 by a family of butchers and cooks in the third generation. The kitchen stresses regional produce and freshness.
new.tip: Try the house-made meat and sausage dishes. Reservations are recommended.

new.title: Eat fish at Fischerhütte on the Edersee
new.desc: The Fischerhütte at Rehbach is a lakeside restaurant with a garden terrace on the Edersee, reached on foot or by boat. It specialises in fish from the lake and nearby waters.
new.tip: Try the trout. Seasonal opening, so check the website fischerhuette-edersee.de first.

new.title: Have a regional dinner at Zum Alten Brauhaus in Hofgeismar
new.desc: Zum Alten Brauhaus on Marktstraße in the old town of Hofgeismar combines a hotel, restaurant and café. Reviewers praise the friendly staff and regional cooking.
new.tip: Eat in the dining room after walking the old town.

new.title: Enjoy seasonal regional food at Rosengarten in Ziegenhain
new.desc: Restaurant Rosengarten in the hotel of the same name in Ziegenhain serves regional, seasonal and vegetarian dishes. Main courses range from roughly 15 to 35 euros.
new.tip: Choose a seasonal regional main course; Sunday hours are shorter.

new.title: Eat Italian-style ice cream at Eis Cafe Mosena in Höxter
new.desc: Eis Cafe Mosena on Marktstraße is a popular gelateria in the old town of Höxter, favoured by locals and visitors.
new.tip: Take a scoop on a walk to the Weser promenade.

new.title: Have coffee and cake at Café Prinzess Emma in Bad Arolsen
new.desc: Café Prinzess Emma on Schloßstraße is a cosy café near the Residenzschloss, named after a princess of Waldeck. It is a meeting place for locals and visitors.
new.tip: Stop in after the palace for coffee and cake.
new.q: Café Prinzess Emma, Schloßstraße 17, Bad Arolsen

new.title: Stop at Café Zur Traube in Melsungen
new.desc: Café and Pension Zur Traube on Brückenstraße is a local café in the old town of Melsungen near the Fulda bridge.
new.tip: Combine coffee with a walk to the half-timbered town hall nearby.

new.title: Spend a day at Tierpark Sababurg
new.desc: Tierpark Sababurg in the Reinhardswald is one of Germany's oldest animal parks, founded in 1571. It covers over 130 hectares of oak avenues and has European and endangered domestic animals.
new.tip: Open all year, longer hours in summer. Adult tickets are about 12 euros.

new.title: Soak in brine at the Weser-Therme in Bad Karlshafen
new.desc: The Weser-Therme offers indoor pools with different salt concentrations at 33 to 36 degrees, fed by Hesse's saltiest thermal brine spring.
new.tip: Open daily, 9:00 to 22:00, Friday and Saturday to 23:00; closed 24 December and New Year's Day.

new.title: Take a boat trip on the Edersee
new.desc: Personenschiffahrt Edersee runs passenger ships such as Stern von Waldeck and Edersee Star from Waldeck Strandbad and the dam. Trips follow the lake past the national park shores.
new.tip: Season runs from about Easter to October. Check the timetable at personenschifffahrt-edersee.de.

new.title: Hike a stage of the Urwaldsteig above the Edersee
new.desc: The Urwaldsteig circles the Edersee in six stages on narrow paths, through oak forests in the northern Naturpark and through the Kellerwald-Edersee National Park to the south. Since 2011 the park's beech forests are part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Ancient Beech Forests.
new.tip: Start in Hemfurth and climb the Große Hegekopf for lake views. Wear hiking boots.

new.title: Walk the Hagenstein route from the Kellerwald national park centre
new.desc: The NationalparkZentrum Kellerwald in Vöhl-Herzhausen opened in 2008 and is the start of the Hagenstein route through the Kellerwald-Edersee National Park. The park, founded in 2004, protects old beech woods.
new.tip: Pick up trail information at the centre before setting out.

new.title: Walk the Baumkronenweg and wildlife park at Edersee
new.desc: The Wildtierpark Edersee near Hemfurth has native wildlife in large enclosures and a treetop walkway through the canopy of the woods above the lake.
new.tip: Combine with a walk down to the lake. Check seasonal hours.

new.title: Ride the Ettelsberg cable car in Willingen
new.desc: The Ettelsberg cable car takes visitors up to the 838-metre summit above Willingen, where there is a wildlife park, a leisure park and hikes over the Hochheide moorland. Near the base is the Mühlenkopfschanze ski jump.
new.tip: Open year round, but weekday service is paused from 2 November to 3 December 2026 for maintenance.

new.title: Hike to the Frau-Holle-Teich on the Hoher Meißner
new.desc: The Frau-Holle-Teich is a protected pond at about 623 metres on the Hoher Meißner and is tied to the Grimm tale of Frau Holle. The Premiumweg P1 loops to the Kasseler Kuppe at 754 metres.
new.tip: Start at the Wanderparkplatz Frau-Holle-Teich. The P1 loop is about 13.7 km and takes four hours.

new.title: Breathe the brine air at the Gradierwerk in Bad Sooden-Allendorf
new.desc: The Gradierwerk in Bad Sooden-Allendorf is one of the last wooden salt-graduation structures in Germany. Brine trickles over thorn brushwood and creates a salty mist for the spa.
new.tip: Free to visit, best on a calm day. The Salzmuseum is nearby.

new.title: See a Festspiele play in the Stiftsruine
new.desc: The Bad Hersfelder Festspiele have staged plays and musicals in the Stiftsruine each summer since 1951. The 2026 jubilee season drew about 85,000 visitors with Parzival and Pippi Langstrumpf.
new.tip: The 2027 season runs from 18 June. Book tickets early.

new.title: Browse the Bartenwetzer market in Melsungen
new.desc: The Marktplatz in Melsungen hosts a weekly market with regional produce on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and a Bartenwetzer Wochenmarkt in the season.
new.tip: Come before noon to see the Bartenwetzer figure on the town hall.

new.title: Hike the Barfußpfad and Seesteine on the Hoher Meißner
new.desc: A circular hike near Meißner-Germerode links the barefoot trail, the Schwalbenthal valley and the Seesteine rock formations on the slopes of the Hoher Meißner.
new.tip: Bring a towel if you want to try the barefoot trail. Check the route description on ich-geh-wandern.de.

new.title: Walk the Grimmsteig from Hessisch Lichtenau to the Hoher Meißner
new.desc: Stage 2 of the Grimmsteig long-distance trail runs from Hessisch Lichtenau up to the Hoher Meißner, linking the sites of the Grimm fairy tales.
new.tip: Plan a full day and check transport back. Details at ich-geh-wandern.de.
